claim_under_test: PSI BCQ and MCQ failures come from losing the identity of the marked pedestrian after the annotation disappears (submitted paper, Section 6).
verdict: Not supported by this case. The model tracked the pedestrian correctly and described exactly the ground-truth option, then failed to emit a parseable answer. This is an output-contract failure, not an identity failure.
evidence_type: held-out PSI training item with real ground truth, scored locally
question_polarity: why the pedestrian might NOT intend to cross

ground_truth.text:
- Pedestrian was standing still and not moving into the roadway.
- Pedestrian remained on the sidewalk.

prediction.note: No 'Final answer: X' line was produced. make_submission.py would substitute the type-correct fallback 'A' for this item at submission time.

what_the_model_actually_saw: The pedestrian marked with the red bounding box is visible at t=0s and remains visible through t=2s. At t=0s, the pedestrian is standing on the sidewalk at the edge of the road, near the curb. ... The pedestrian does not move into the roadway; they remain on the sidewalk throughout the clip.
diagnosis: The opening description is correct and matches ground-truth option D almost word for word: standing still, on the sidewalk, not entering the roadway.

The routed prompt then asks the model to eliminate every option containing a false claim. The model negates each option in turn and mis-negates the correct one: 'The pedestrian is not standing still and not moving into the roadway; they are standing still on the sidewalk at the edge of the road.' The double negative rules out the option its own description supports.

The elimination pass then loops, repeating three earlier sentences nearly verbatim, and the generation is cut off mid-sentence at 1497 characters ('...they are not on the far-left/opposite side,') before reaching the required final line.
Identity was never lost. Geometry was never needed. The failure is entirely in the answer-formatting contract that the paper lists as a system contribution.

population_statistics.note: Items with no parseable final letter, on the ambiguous-split held-out sample.
population_statistics.interpretation: Between 15% and 25% of generations on this sample produce no parseable answer under every prompt program tried. These items are silently converted to a fallback letter, so they are scored as ordinary wrong answers rather than surfacing as contract violations.
population_statistics.caveat: The PSI 'ambiguous' split is deliberately the hard subset — annotators disagreed on these clips. These rates are not the rate on the official test set, where MCQ accuracy was 0.6044.

related_ablation: ABLATIONS.md section A2. On the paired 24-item subset the routed prompt scored 3/24 against the generic prompt's 8/24, losing every discordant pair 5-0.
frame_rendering: Frames are not committed — PSI-VQA inherits the TASI Benchmark Data Sharing Agreement. Render locally with scripts/render_case_studies.py --data-root track3_anomaly/data/psi_vqa.
